evidence: Summit Chief has one documented North Face route: the Haley/Burdick April 2004 snow-and-ice line (Grade III, WI3, ~2,000 ft, 12 pitches). This row is an empty shell (no overview, beta or FA) of the same climb filed under a second spelling of the peak; keep the richer Summit Chief Mountain row and fold the 12-pitch count in. The two areas (wa_summit_chief / wa_summit_chief_mountain) are the same peak and should be merged too.

Same climb as wa_summit_chief_north_face (Haley/Burdick 2004, WI2-3 ramp, snowfields, AI2 exit). This is the row to keep: it carries the overview, beta, breakdown and FA; take pitches=12 from the other row.

The Fin's only documented route is the Northeast Face: one 120-ft 5.4 pitch into a chockstone chimney, then a third-class scramble to the summit, FA Harold Pinsch and Garry Tate 1966. This row has that exact grade, face, FA and description under a generic 'Sawtooth Range Scramble' name; there is no separate scramble route to The Fin.

The Incisor (7,440 ft, FA 1958) is a Needles summit above Royal Basin. The row's own rock_grade records its single route as 5.4 along the knife-edge ridge (the Olympic climbing guide's line, per an earlier audit in this repo), so 'The Needles Scramble' names a scramble that does not exist. No online page names the route, so 'Knife-Edge Ridge' is descriptive. The beta's generic 'Class 3-5.8 somewhere on the massif' text should be replaced with the ridge line.

The documented route to The Temple's summit is the West Side: two pitches, Grade II+, 5.6, with a bolt protecting a steep friction face, matching this row's grade, pitch count, bolt and its own face field. No source describes a 'South Ridge' route on The Temple; Beckey's 1942 first ascent gives an easiest route of 5.3, consistent with the 5.3-5.6 range here. The overview's 'south side' wording should follow the rename.

The beta (Bird Creek Camp, shoulder of the south ridge, into the east basin, zigzag ledges up the face to a 5.2-5.4 crux) is the East Face, the standard route since Liebert and Grubenhoff's 1982 first ascent. The Darr 1940 FA on this row belongs to the West Face, a different and essentially unrepeated line, so it must not move to the East Face page; 'South Ridge' is only the approach shoulder.

The Classic Route (5.4) is Unicorn's standard climb: Snow Lake trail, gully to the saddle west of the peak, around the summit block and up its south side for a short low-5th pitch. This row describes exactly that line under an approach name; fold its approach and summit-horn beta into wa_classic_route_2. Open Book and The Roof (5.6) remain separate summit-block variations.

The only ice line documented at Black Ice Crag (Exit 38) is CYA, listed in the Washington Ice guidebook as WI4 M4, about 30 m. This empty row named 'unknown' carries that exact WI4 M4 grade and one pitch, so it is an import placeholder for CYA. CYA's own row should take the M4.

Ragged Edge (II 5.7, 6 pitches, FA Darin Berdinka and Gene Pires, August 18, 2013) is one route on the right side of Vesper's north face; both rows carry identical pitch grades and FA. Keep wa_ragged_edge, which uses the route's actual name, and take alpine_grade II from this row.

Whatcom Peak's south-side route (South Spur) is reached from Whatcom Pass by a low orbit of the peak on the east, across the slabs below the Whatcom Glacier, or from Easy Ridge to Perfect Pass. From Perfect Pass parties climb the south snowfields and a short 3rd-class scramble. This row describes exactly that orbit plus the Perfect Pass finish, so it is the South Spur by one of its two approaches; keep it as approach beta on wa_south_spur. The 1936 Berry/Buchanan FA belongs to the North Ridge row, not here.

The Northwest Shoulder is Whitehorse's standard route and is itself a snow and glacier climb: Niederprum Trail, couloir to Lone Tree Pass, High Pass, the So-Bahli-Ahli (Whitehorse) Glacier and a short exposed rock finish, usually done in spring. This row is that same line under early-season conditions, not a separate Northwest Face route. Fold its snow, rollover and ski-descent notes into the NW Shoulder page as conditions beta.

Mountain Project lists one Witches Tower route, the East Face: 4th class, 1-2 pitches, with an Ice 2/Mixed 1b note. That matches this row's grade, the zig-zag ledges and the ice-step remark. 'E/SE' blurs it with the separate Southeast Face, so rename it East Face.

The 'NE Buttress' (V, 5.8, AI2: brushy lower buttress, rock band to a ~7,100 ft bivy, snow arete, an ice pitch) is the full modern line up the NE rib system. It follows the more prominent right-hand 1957 (Western Rib) start, while the 1951 route takes the left rib and is a separate line, so that sibling stays. Fix this row's fa so it no longer claims the 1951 history: it should name the 1957 Western Rib first ascent (party not found online).

Little Tahoma's standard route is the East Shoulder, climbed by way of the Fryingpan and Whitman glaciers from Summerland (Grade II+, steep snow, loose summit rock; first ascent Flett and Garrison, August 29, 1894). Mountain Project calls it 'Frying Pan / Whitman Glaciers' and The Mountaineers call it 'East Shoulder', but it is one climb. Keep the East Shoulder row and fold in this row's richer beta.
